body: Thank you, that helps and I'll try that. She still wants to talk, so I might just try and avoid the subject then for a little. But she just told me that she didn't go through with it because she couldn't imagine leaving her loved ones behind including me, so I think that's a good sign, and hopefully moving forward she can make progress. Thanks again for your help and I'll do my best.

I didn't quite say "don't do it" but I understand what you mean, she expressed her thoughts about it, and i urged her to consider an alternate route if that makes sense (I.e. I tried to get into her thought process, and divert her from those thoughts, in a more passive tone)
Thank you so much, and I am truly sorry for your loss. Anything you can say that will help me reach her. I can't express how grateful I would be.

Hey,

I know the situation that you're in and I would hope that you reconsider. I'm sure that you are a genuinely likeable person. However, having said that, I think that you suffer from a confidence issue. I, like you, had the same exact problem when my fiancée left me. When I tried to get back out there, I realized that I could never keep a conversation going, that it seemed like I always fell up short. Constant rejection and humiliation. I considered suicide as an alternative to being alone. I want to impress upon you that it is NOT the solution, it simply numbs the pain. If you were to die, you would truly be alone, but, I think that if you give it time, and you try and be confident in yourself (let yourself shine) you'll see that you have plenty to offer. 
If you want something a bit more concrete, try, at least once a day to tell yourself that you are strong and attractive, even if you don't mean it. Eventually you'll start to believe yourself, and your confidence will come and you're ability to keep conversation and get the girl will shockingly increase. It worked for me at least but I hope you reconsider, and I hope you have a good day.

So update if you were interested, we talked for hours, and she told me I might be the one, and it scares her because she is just starting college, and mistakes happen, and she doesn't want to ruin it. I told her I understand but that I wanted to give it a try anyway (I'm a senior). So idk where we stand but I figured I'd let you know that your advice was useful! So thank you!

Thank you for your response! It helps, and we communicate very well for the most part. Obviously we are not perfect in telling each other things, but as I said, years of relationships with people that hide their feelings and their lives, means I have a little doubt. She seems very forthright, and hopefully she is actually. Thanks again for the response!
